resolution.gpt_rationale: For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may bring an action for summary possession only if the tenant’s failure to pay continues for 5 days after the landlord gives written notice demanding payment. Thus, Delaware requires a 5-day written notice before filing the eviction action.
resolution.gemini_rationale: A landlord must give a tenant written notice demanding payment of rent, and the tenant must be given a period of not less than 5 days to pay the amount due. Only after this period has expired without payment may the landlord terminate the rental agreement and file an action for summary possession.

flags.gemini_reasoning: Effective October 1, 2023, 25 Del. C. § 5113 became the controlling statute for serving residential notices, superseding older general provisions. It explicitly outlines methods for personal service (§ 5113(a)(1)), substituted service (§ 5113(a)(2)), and mail/posting (§ 5113(a)(3)-(4)), with the latter being permissible only after due diligence attempts at personal or substituted service (§ 5113(b)). The GPT model's citations are the most accurate reflection of this current law.

federal.effect: During active moratorium periods: 30-day notice required before filing; no fees or penalties for nonpayment during moratorium. federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)

elements_confirmed: The landlord, or someone acting on the landlord's behalf, committed an act or omission which substantially interfered with the tenant's use and enjoyment of the premises.
The interference is so severe as to render the premises unfit for the purposes for which it was leased, amounting to a constructive eviction.
The tenant provided notice to the landlord of the interference and the landlord failed to remedy it.
The tenant vacated the premises within a reasonable time after the landlord's failure to remedy.
